sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 24.10.2016 passed by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambah, District Morena (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 83/2010, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambah, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of the accident, the issue of negligence, and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality and are not under challenge in the present appeal.

3. As per the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal, on account of the permanent disability sustained by the claimant Rakesh Singh in the motor accident, compensation to the tune of Rs.
6,30,250/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization has been awarded.

4. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellant/claimant has preferred the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4575 2 MA-124-2017 present appeal contending that the learned Claims Tribunal has passed the award without proper appreciation of the evidence and the settled Rakesh Singh Tomar vs Sahdev Singh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7179378/
1 principles of law.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that at the time of the accident, the claimant was working as a Havaldar in the Indian Army and was earning Rs. 22,000/- per month.
It is further contended that as a result of the accident, the claimant sustained permanent disability, which led to his termination from service.

It is urged that the Claims Tribunal committed an error in assessing only 15%
permanent disability in relation to his earning capacity and further erred in not awarding compensation towards future prospects.
On these grounds, it is prayed that a just and reasonable enhancement in the amount of compensation be granted.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3-Insurance Company supported the impugned award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation on the basis of the evidence available on record.
It is contended that the appeal is devoid of merit and deserves to be dismissed.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
Upon consideration of the evidence available on record, it is found that the claimant sustained 40% permanent physical disability in the motor accident.
At the relevant time, he was serving as a Havaldar in the Indian Army and was earning Rs. 22,000/- per month.
It is further evident that after suffering the disability, the claimant was terminated from his service in the Indian Army.

However, it has also come on record that thereafter he was employed as a Security Guard and continued to earn his livelihood.
8.
In view of the aforesaid facts, it is clear that the claimant was not rendered totally incapacitated from performing any work.

Since he was able to engage in alternative employment and earn income,
the learned Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the loss of earning capacity at 15% despite the physical disability being 40%.
This finding is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4575 3 MA-124-2017 based on proper appreciation of evidence and does not call for any interference by this Court.

9. On perusal of the record, this Court further finds that the Claims Tribunal has correctly assessed the monthly income of the claimant at Rs. 22,000/-.
10.

As regards loss of future income, in light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimant is entitled to addition towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the claimant was in permanent employment,
future prospects are required to be added at the rate of 50%.
11.

Further, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another , reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, considering the age of the claimant, the appropriate multiplier applicable in the present case is 15.
12.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another , reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant, as well as the pain and suffering, expenses towards special diet, attendant charges, and travelling expenses incurred due to the accident, this Court finds it appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs. 1,50,000/- under Rakesh Singh Tomar vs Sahdev Singh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7179378/
2 these conventional heads.
13.

entities.text: Rakesh Singh Tomar vs Sahdev Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMO  Income Rs. 22,000 X 12= 2,
 Future Prospects@50% Rs.1,32,000/-
 Loss of earning @15% Rs.59,400/-
 Multiplier 15 Rs.8,91,000/-
 Other Heads Rs.1,50,000/-
 Total Compensation = Rs.10,41,000/-
14.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4575 4 MA-124-2017 comes to Rs.10,41,000/- as against the sum of Rs.6,30,250/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.4,10,750/-/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
15. Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, and the compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.4,10,750/-.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellant within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

16. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellant shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
17. In view of the foregoing discussion, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellant/claimant stands disposed of accordingly.
